get.description: Returns who the API key or OAuth token belongs to, the plan it is on and this month's credit usage. Costs no credits and does not count against the search rate limit.

auth_type.description: How this request was authenticated: api_key, oauth or session.

plan.description: A plan name, or credits:N for N thousand credits a month.

month.description: The calendar month the usage figures cover, YYYY-MM in UTC.

monthly_credits.description: Credits included each month. 0 on Free, which is a one-time grant instead.

one_time_credits.description: Free only: the one-time credits the account started with (1,000; more if support added some). They do not renew. Null on paid plans.

credits_used.description: Paid: credits used this month. Free: credits used of the one-time grant.

credits_remaining.description: Paid: left of this month's allowance. Free: left of the one-time grant.

extra_credits.description: One-time credits bought on top of the plan, drawn after the monthly allowance.

post.summary: Tell JobsPipe what was wrong or missing
post.description: Send a report about the data or the tools: a posting that is closed or stale, a wrong field, a search that missed what exists, a dataset gap, a confusing tool. A person reads every submission. Costs no credits and does not count against the search rate limit. Up to 10 a minute and 100 a day per account.

message.description: What was wrong, missing or confusing, in the agent's own words.

job_ids.description: The postings the report is about, by the id a search or fetch returned.

tool.description: The tool or endpoint that was being used.

query.description: The search input that was run, as it was given, so a miss can be replayed.

agent.description: The client or model sending the report.

source.description: Where a person sent the report from, when it was not an agent. Stored as the agent when none is given.

reason.description: What is wrong with the postings in `job_ids`, as a fixed reason. Stored at the head of the message.

post.description: Returns a Stripe link where the account holder buys a package, or confirms a move to a larger one. Nothing is charged or changed by this call; the new allowance applies once the account holder completes the Stripe page. A smaller package is refused with 409: downgrades are made on the billing page. Send a package, or credits, or nothing to be offered the package that covers 1.5x this month's use.

package.description: The package to buy: seeker, builder, growth, scale, business. Wins over credits when both are sent.

credits.description: Monthly credits wanted; the smallest package that covers them is chosen. Above 500,000 is an Enterprise plan.

200.description: A link to pay or confirm.

url.description: Where the account holder pays or confirms the change. Open it in a browser.

flow.description: checkout: a Stripe Checkout page for a new subscription. portal: a Stripe page where the account holder confirms the move to the larger package.

credits.description: Credits a month on the chosen package.

billing_interval.description: How the package is billed: the account's current interval (a yearly subscriber stays yearly; credits still refresh every month). New purchases here are monthly; yearly is chosen on the billing page.

price_usd.description: The package's price in USD per billing_interval.

400.description: Unknown package, bad credits, or more than the largest package.

403.description: The caller is a member of a workspace that pays for them; only its owner or admin can change its plan (billing_managers_only).

409.description: The account already holds that package (already_subscribed), or asked for a smaller one (downgrade_requires_dashboard: made on the billing page, billing_url).

502.description: Stripe could not start the checkout.

post.description: Monitors a list of records and sends their events to one of your webhooks until the monitor expires. A job monitor sends job.closed when a job in it closes. The ids are looked up, so the response also says, for free, which are already closed and which match nothing; neither is added. Costs no credits.

ids.description: Record ids as search returned them, up to 1000 per request.

events.description: Events to send. Default: every event of the type ("job.closed").

expires_in_days.description: How many days the monitor runs, a whole number from 1 to 365. Default 90.

402.description: Monitors need the Builder package or above, or the plan's monitoring limit would be passed.

404.description: No such monitor or webhook on this account.

post.description: Search live job postings from 30+ sources, normalized into a single schema.

limit.description: Max results to return. Capped by your plan's page size.

include_technologies.description: Add `technologies`, the graded list of technologies each posting names, to every job. Off by default, and the field is then absent. Each returned job that names at least one technology costs 1 extra credit on top of the job's own credit, once per job per calendar month (UTC); jobs with none cost nothing extra.

blur_company_data.description: DEPRECATED and ignored. Preview mode has been removed: every search now returns unmasked records and is billed at one credit per job returned. Still accepted so existing integrations keep working; it has no effect on the response or the price.

job_title_or.description: Match jobs whose title contains any of these.

job_title_not.description: Exclude jobs whose title contains any of these.

description_or.description: Match jobs whose description contains any of these (e.g. a skill or tech).

description_not.description: Exclude jobs whose description contains any of these.

employment_type_or.description: Match any employment type: full-time, part-time, contract, temporary, internship.

language_or.description: Match postings WRITTEN in any of these languages, as lowercase ISO 639-1 codes, e.g. ["en"] or ["en","sv"]. This is the language of the posting text, not of the country: 18.3% of Swedish postings and 17.7% of German ones are in English, and Canada is 84.5% English with the rest French. Use it to fetch only the roles your team can actually read when hiring across a multilingual market. Postings we have not labelled never match - add include_unknown: ["language"] to keep them. Values that are not exactly two letters are ignored.

language_not.description: Exclude postings written in any of these languages, as lowercase ISO 639-1 codes, e.g. ["fr"]. Postings we have not labelled are kept, so this narrows by known language rather than requiring one.

source_or.description: Match any collector source/platform (OR). Job boards: linkedin, indeed, cvlibrary, resumelibrary, ycombinator, arbeitnow, himalayas, jobicy, themuse, remoteok, workingnomads, landingjobs, remotive, rise, bayt. Public employment services: eures, jobtech. ATS (company career sites): greenhouse, workday, ashby, lever, workable, recruitee, personio, smartrecruiters, breezy, paylocity, manatal, jobscore, teamtailor, pinpoint, hirehive. Case, spaces and punctuation are ignored ("CV-Library" = cvlibrary); aliases: yc for ycombinator, breezyhr for breezy. An unrecognized source matches nothing.

source_not.description: Exclude these collector sources. Same accepted values and aliases as source_or; an unrecognized source excludes nothing.

job_country_code_or.description: Match any of these ISO country codes, e.g. ["US","GB"].

job_location_or.description: Match jobs whose city or region contains any of these, e.g. ["Seattle","WA"]. Metro wrappers are stripped ("Greater London" also matches London), and a US state, Canadian province or UK nation by name matches every spelling of it ("Pennsylvania" also matches PA). Terms of three characters or fewer are codes or exact names and match whole values (WA is Washington state, never Iowa); a country code or name matches the whole country. Combine with job_country_code_or to disambiguate same-named cities. For a city by name, city_or is the precise filter.

city_or.description: Whole city names, e.g. ["London","Munich"]. Case-insensitive, and a metro wrapper on the stored value is ignored ("Greater London" and "London Area" are London). Spellings and diacritics are normalised for cities we know: "München" finds Munich, "Cracow" finds Kraków. Other cities match the stored value exactly. Combine with job_country_code_or to disambiguate same-named cities; use job_location_or for substring matching.

posted_at_max_age_days.description: Only postings newer than this many days.

posted_at_gte.description: Only postings on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

posted_at_lte.description: Only postings on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

discovered_at_gte.description: Only postings first discovered by JobsPipe at or after this UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS). Tracks when we first saw the posting, not when it was posted; use it to poll for new jobs without re-reading the corpus.

company_name_or.description: Match any of these company names (exact).

company_name_partial_match_or.description: Match any of these company names (partial).

company_technology_slug_or.description: Beta. Only jobs at companies whose postings show they use any of these technologies (evidence tier likely or confirmed), e.g. ["snowflake", "dbt"]. At most 10 slugs. Returns 400 until the filter is enabled for the API.

min_employee_count.description: Only jobs at companies with at least this many employees. Uses the exact headcount where known, otherwise the lower bound of the company's size band.

max_employee_count.description: Only jobs at companies with at most this many employees. Uses the exact headcount where known; a company known only by a size band matches when the band starts at or below this number.

include_unknown_size.description: Also return jobs at companies whose employee count is unknown. Size data covers roughly half the corpus, and min/max_employee_count exclude every unknown-size company by default.

min_revenue_usd.description: Only jobs at companies whose estimated annual revenue, in US dollars, is at least this amount (the published revenue_usd). Companies with no revenue on record are excluded unless include_unknown contains "company_revenue".

max_revenue_usd.description: Only jobs at companies whose estimated annual revenue, in US dollars, is at most this amount (the published revenue_usd). Companies with no revenue on record are excluded unless include_unknown contains "company_revenue".

lei_or.description: Legal Entity Identifiers (ISO 17442). Matches jobs at a company with one of these LEIs or at any company in the corporate group the LEI heads. 1 to 50 LEIs of 20 letters and digits, e.g. ["5493001KJTIIGC8Y1R12"]; case is ignored, and a comma-separated string is accepted. Jobs at companies without a known LEI never match.

company_key_or.description: Company ids from the Companies endpoints (the key of a row of POST /v1/jobs/companies, or of a company profile). Matches only jobs at exactly these companies: unlike company_name_or, a name is never matched as a prefix, so Apple's id never brings in Apple Bank. 1 to 50 ids as strings of digits, e.g. ["14189461223778919517"]; a comma-separated string is accepted.

company_hq_country_or.description: Only jobs at companies headquartered in one of these countries, as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, e.g. ["US","DE"]. This is where the company is based, not where the job is: combine with job_country_code_or for "German companies hiring in the US". Case is ignored and a comma-separated string is accepted. Companies with no known headquarters never match.

company_hq_country_not.description: Only jobs at companies headquartered outside these countries (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2). Companies with no known headquarters never match.

include_unlabeled_employment_type.description: Also return jobs whose employment type is unknown. About 27% of postings do not state one, and employment_type_or excludes every one of them by default.

job_seniority_or.description: Match any of these seniority levels.

include_unlabeled_seniority.description: Also return jobs whose seniority is unknown. About 55% of postings do not state a level, and job_seniority_or excludes every one of them by default.

skills_or.description: Match jobs tagged with any of these skill slugs (e.g. ["python", "kubernetes"]). Skills are extracted from title + description against a curated lexicon.

occupation_code_or.description: Match any of these ISCO-08 occupation codes. 4-digit codes match exactly (e.g. "2512" Software Developers); 1-3 digit codes match as hierarchy prefixes (e.g. "25" = all ICT professionals).

isic_division_or.description: Match employers in any of these ISIC Rev.4 industry divisions (2-digit, e.g. "62" Computer programming and consultancy).

region_or.description: US states and Canadian provinces as ISO 3166-2 codes, e.g. ["US-NY", "CA-ON"]. Qualified by country because the underlying column stores "CA" for California while "CA" is also Canada's country code. Matches every spelling a job board publishes, so "CA-ON" finds both "ON" and "Ontario".

employer_type_or.description: Match only these employer types. "employer" hires for itself, "agency" is a staffing or recruitment firm posting for a client, "broker" is a job board republishing another company's listing. Selecting "employer" also returns jobs whose employer has not been classified yet.

employer_type_not.description: Exclude these employer types. Unclassified employers are never excluded, so ["agency","broker"] returns direct employers plus jobs whose employer has not been classified yet - the same set as employer_type_or ["employer"].

remote.description: true for remote-only, false to exclude remote.

work_arrangement_or.description: Match any of "remote", "hybrid" or "onsite". Finer than `remote`, which answers false for hybrid and onsite alike. Jobs whose arrangement is unknown never match.

job_id_or.description: Return jobs matching any of these IDs.

job_ids.description: Look up a specific set of job IDs.

status.description: Filter by lifecycle: active (default, still open), closed, or any.

visa_sponsorship_or.description: Match any of these visa stances, parsed from the posting text: "offers" (sponsorship available), "no" (explicitly not available), "citizenship_required" (citizenship or security clearance required). Jobs that say nothing never match.

benefits_or.description: Match jobs advertising any of these benefit slugs, e.g. ["401k", "health_insurance", "paid_time_off"] (any spelling: "health insurance" works too). Benefits come from structured board data (Indeed today), so coverage is partial; see metadata.field_coverage.

metro_code_or.description: Match any of these US CBSA metro codes (e.g. "35620" New York). Resolved from the job's city/region; non-US jobs never match.

max_applicant_count.description: Only jobs with at most this many applicants. Applicant counts exist only where the source exposes them (LinkedIn), so this filter also drops every job without a count.

has_recruiter_email.description: true for only jobs with a recruiter contact email parsed from the posting, false for only jobs without one.

min_salary_usd.description: Only jobs whose posted salary reaches this annual USD amount (the max of the posted range, annualized). Jobs without a posted salary never match; estimated salaries are not consulted.

max_ghost_score.description: Exclude jobs whose ghost-likelihood score (0-100) exceeds this. Unscored jobs always pass: the filter drops known-likely ghost jobs, it does not require a score.

esco_skill_id_or.description: Match jobs tagged with any of these ESCO skill concept IDs (exact match). See each job's esco_skills for the id/label pairs.

include_unknown.description: Also match jobs whose value is UNKNOWN for these fields, e.g. ["seniority", "location"]. Without it every filter drops unknowns: a job with no seniority never matches job_seniority_or. "location" widens region_or within each subdivision's country, and job_location_or only when job_country_code_or is set. include_unknown_size, include_unlabeled_seniority and include_unlabeled_employment_type are aliases of "company_size", "seniority" and "employment_type".

last_verified_max_age_days.description: Only jobs seen on their source (or re-written) within this many days. Active jobs are closed when a re-check finds them gone, and re-checks take time; this drops the ones we have not confirmed recently.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from metadata.next_cursor to fetch the next page.

delta_cursor.description: Opaque cursor from metadata.next_delta_cursor. Returns only postings JobsPipe first discovered since that cursor was issued, so a repeating query reads new jobs instead of the whole result set again. Keep the rest of the filters identical between calls. Supersedes discovered_at_gte when both are sent. The bound is inclusive to the second, so a posting discovered in the boundary second can repeat once; it is not billed twice in the same calendar month.

order_by.description: Sort order. Only [{"field":"posted_at","desc":true}] is supported, which is how every response is already sorted; anything else is rejected rather than silently ignored.

schema.description: Job search filters. All fields optional; combine with AND. Unknown parameters are rejected with HTTP 400.

total_results.description: Total matches, or null unless include_total_results was set.

truncated_results.description: Jobs returned in this data array.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or null if no more results.

next_delta_cursor.description: Pass as delta_cursor on the next run of this same query to get only postings discovered since now. Null while next_cursor is set: the watermark is only meaningful once you have read the whole result set, so finish paging first and use the cursor from the last page.

credits_charged.description: Credits this call cost. One credit buys a job for the rest of the calendar month (UTC), so this is the number of jobs in data that the account had not already paid for this month, plus technologies_credits_charged when include_technologies was set.

jobs_already_paid.description: Jobs in data that cost nothing because the account already paid for them this month. Without include_technologies, credits_charged plus jobs_already_paid equals the number of jobs returned.

technologies_credits_charged.description: Present only with include_technologies. The part of credits_charged spent on technologies: 1 per returned job that names at least one technology and whose technologies the account had not already paid for this month.

technologies_already_paid.description: Present only with include_technologies. Jobs whose technologies cost nothing because the account already paid for them this month. technologies_credits_charged plus technologies_already_paid equals the number of returned jobs that name a technology.

credits_remaining.description: Credits the account can still spend after this call: what is left of the monthly allowance plus extra credits, or on Free what is left of the one-time grant.

credits_allowance.description: What credits_remaining is measured against: the monthly allowance on a paid package, the one-time grant on Free.

field_coverage.description: For each filter the request used that reads a partially filled field: the share (0-100) of active postings from the last 30 days that carry the field, overall and per source. Use it to tell 'no matches' from 'field unknown'; include_unknown widens the filter.

id.description: Stable JobsPipe ID. Stable for a given posting over time, so it can be stored and re-looked-up. NOT shared across sources: the same role posted to two boards is keyed per source and gets two IDs.

final_url.description: Always null - use url or source_url.

founded.description: Year the company was founded, where known.

revenue_usd.description: Most recent known annual revenue, converted to US dollars. Null when no figure is known.

revenue_year.description: Fiscal year the revenue figure refers to.

revenue_source.description: Short identifier of where the revenue figure came from, such as a business register, a securities filing or a company directory.

revenue_confidence.description: How the revenue figure was obtained, strongest first: filed = taken from the company's statutory accounts; reported = stated by the company itself; band = only an estimated range is known; revenue_usd is a representative figure within it; derived = estimated from funding or valuation; extracted = read from public text about the company.

entity_kind.description: What kind of organisation the employer is: company, branch, public_sector or staffing_agency.

founded_year.description: Year the legal entity was founded or registered.

headcount.description: Employee count as filed, registered or listed in a company directory. Can differ from company_object.employee_count, which comes from the company's public profile.

industry.description: Industry as recorded for the legal entity or, where no record exists, the industry a company directory lists.

hq_region.description: Region or state of the employer's headquarters, as written by the source (for example California), when known.

hq_city.description: City of the employer's headquarters, when known.

revenue_low_usd.description: Lower bound of the revenue, in US dollars: the range behind the figure when the source gave one; null otherwise.

revenue_high_usd.description: Upper bound of the revenue, in US dollars: the range behind the figure when the source gave one; null otherwise.

headcount_low.description: Lower bound of the headcount: the range behind the figure when the source gave one; null otherwise.

headcount_high.description: Upper bound of the headcount: the range behind the figure when the source gave one; null otherwise.

lei.description: The company's Legal Entity Identifier (ISO 17442), 20 characters. Null when we have not identified the company's legal entity.

legal_name.description: The registered legal name of the entity `lei` identifies. Null when `lei` is null.

group_lei.description: The LEI of the corporate group the company belongs to: its ultimate parent, or its direct parent when no ultimate parent is recorded. Null when the company has no recorded parent, or when `lei` is null. Can equal `lei` when the company heads its own group.

group_name.description: The registered legal name of the entity `group_lei` identifies. Null when `group_lei` is null.

intelligence.description: Revenue, legal identity and entity type of the employer. Null when no record exists for the company in the posting's country or the record holds no finding, and always null on GET /v1/companies/{key}, which has no posting country to resolve against.

company_object.description: Structured details about the hiring company. Every field is independently optional.

closed_reason.description: Why it closed: closed, gone, or stale.

has_blurred_data.description: DEPRECATED. Always false: preview mode has been removed and every record is returned unmasked. Kept so clients reading the field keep parsing.

technology_slugs.description: The older, ungraded technology list, kept for compatibility. Prefer `technologies`.

slug.description: Taxonomy slug, e.g. "snowflake" or ".net". Filter companies with it via the technographics endpoints.

kind.description: product, language, framework, methodology, certification or standard.

parent_category.description: e.g. "Software and tools". Empty string when unknown.

logo.description: Absolute URL of the technology's logo; null when there is none.

strength.description: How the posting asks for it: a requirement, a nice-to-have, or a mention.

confidence.description: high when independent checks agree the posting names it; medium when it is required or in the title; low otherwise.

sections.description: Posting sections it appears in, e.g. ["requirements"].

in_title.description: Whether the job title names it.

terms.description: Case-insensitive text forms that find the mention in `description`.

items.description: One technology a posting names, graded.

technologies.description: Beta. Technologies the posting names, graded by strength and confidence. Present only when the request set include_technologies, and then on every job; empty until the posting has been extracted. Sorted required, preferred, mentioned; then confidence high to low; then name.

employer_type.description: Who posted this job: "employer" (hires for itself), "agency" (staffing or recruitment firm posting on a client's behalf) or "broker" (job board republishing another company's listing). Defaults to "employer" where the company has not been classified.

work_arrangement.description: One of "remote", "hybrid" or "onsite". Finer than `remote`, which answers false for hybrid and onsite alike. Null where the arrangement is unknown, which is most of the corpus while backfill and re-ingestion catch up.

is_manager.description: Whether the role manages people. `seniority` maps our lead bucket to "director", which files staff and principal individual contributors under a value that reads as people management; this tells them apart.

last_seen_at.description: When we last saw the posting live, on a collection run or a recheck. Usually null once closed. Format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS (UTC).

verified_at.description: When we last updated the posting's status: a collection run, a recheck or a close. Format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS (UTC).

sources.description: Every source this posting was seen on. Normally a single entry, since jobs are keyed per source.

work_arrangement_source.description: How work_arrangement was decided: "source" (declared by the job board) or "text" (parsed from the description).

visa_sponsorship.description: Visa stance parsed from the posting: "offers", "no" or "citizenship_required". Null where the posting says nothing.

benefits.description: Benefit slugs from structured source data. Empty where the source exposes none.

salary_source.description: Where the salary came from: "source" (structured data from the board) or "description" (parsed from the posting text).

salary_type.description: "observed" when the posting itself carries pay, "estimated" when only the corpus benchmark does, null when neither.

estimated_min_annual_salary_usd.description: 25th-percentile annual USD pay for this occupation and location, from public salary statistics. A benchmark, not the employer's posted pay; published beside any observed salary.

expires_at.description: Application deadline where the source publishes one. Format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS (UTC).

applicant_count.description: Number of applicants where the source exposes it (LinkedIn).

recruiter_emails.description: Recruiter contact emails parsed from the posting text.

listing_type.description: How the posting was listed where the source exposes it.

metro_code.description: US CBSA metro code resolved from the job's location. Null outside covered metros.

metro_label.description: Metro display name for metro_code, e.g. "New York-Newark-Jersey City, NY-NJ".

seniority_source.description: How seniority was decided: "source", "title" or "onet_prior" (occupation-level prior).

esco_skills.description: ESCO skill concepts for this job's extracted skills, as stable id/label pairs.

ghost_score.description: 0-100 likelihood the posting is stale or evergreen rather than a live vacancy, from repost cadence, tenure and content signals. Null until scored.

language.description: The language the posting text is written in, as a lowercase ISO 639-1 code, e.g. "en", "sv", "de". The language of the posting, not of the country it is in. Null until the posting has been labelled.

post.summary: Companies hiring for a job search
post.description: The companies behind the jobs that match a job search, one row per company with its matching job count, organised as corporate groups (parent entity, subsidiaries, their subsidiaries). Costs one credit per company returned; parent entities without matching jobs of their own are free, and a company already paid for this calendar month is free.

limit.description: Companies to return, 25 by default. Capped by your plan's page size.

offset.description: Companies to skip (offset pagination, at most 10,000).

job_title_or.description: Match jobs whose title contains any of these.

job_title_not.description: Exclude jobs whose title contains any of these.

description_or.description: Match jobs whose description contains any of these (e.g. a skill or tech).

description_not.description: Exclude jobs whose description contains any of these.

employment_type_or.description: Match any employment type: full-time, part-time, contract, temporary, internship.

language_or.description: Match postings WRITTEN in any of these languages, as lowercase ISO 639-1 codes, e.g. ["en"] or ["en","sv"]. This is the language of the posting text, not of the country: 18.3% of Swedish postings and 17.7% of German ones are in English, and Canada is 84.5% English with the rest French. Use it to fetch only the roles your team can actually read when hiring across a multilingual market. Postings we have not labelled never match - add include_unknown: ["language"] to keep them. Values that are not exactly two letters are ignored.

language_not.description: Exclude postings written in any of these languages, as lowercase ISO 639-1 codes, e.g. ["fr"]. Postings we have not labelled are kept, so this narrows by known language rather than requiring one.

source_or.description: Match any collector source/platform (OR). Job boards: linkedin, indeed, cvlibrary, resumelibrary, ycombinator, arbeitnow, himalayas, jobicy, themuse, remoteok, workingnomads, landingjobs, remotive, rise, bayt. Public employment services: eures, jobtech. ATS (company career sites): greenhouse, workday, ashby, lever, workable, recruitee, personio, smartrecruiters, breezy, paylocity, manatal, jobscore, teamtailor, pinpoint, hirehive. Case, spaces and punctuation are ignored ("CV-Library" = cvlibrary); aliases: yc for ycombinator, breezyhr for breezy. An unrecognized source matches nothing.

source_not.description: Exclude these collector sources. Same accepted values and aliases as source_or; an unrecognized source excludes nothing.

job_country_code_or.description: Match any of these ISO country codes, e.g. ["US","GB"].

job_location_or.description: Match jobs whose city or region contains any of these, e.g. ["Seattle","WA"]. Metro wrappers are stripped ("Greater London" also matches London), and a US state, Canadian province or UK nation by name matches every spelling of it ("Pennsylvania" also matches PA). Terms of three characters or fewer are codes or exact names and match whole values (WA is Washington state, never Iowa); a country code or name matches the whole country. Combine with job_country_code_or to disambiguate same-named cities. For a city by name, city_or is the precise filter.

city_or.description: Whole city names, e.g. ["London","Munich"]. Case-insensitive, and a metro wrapper on the stored value is ignored ("Greater London" and "London Area" are London). Spellings and diacritics are normalised for cities we know: "München" finds Munich, "Cracow" finds Kraków. Other cities match the stored value exactly. Combine with job_country_code_or to disambiguate same-named cities; use job_location_or for substring matching.

posted_at_max_age_days.description: Only postings newer than this many days.

posted_at_gte.description: Only postings on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

posted_at_lte.description: Only postings on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

discovered_at_gte.description: Only postings first discovered by JobsPipe at or after this UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS). Tracks when we first saw the posting, not when it was posted; use it to poll for new jobs without re-reading the corpus.

company_name_or.description: Match any of these company names (exact).

company_name_partial_match_or.description: Match any of these company names (partial).

company_technology_slug_or.description: Beta. Only jobs at companies whose postings show they use any of these technologies (evidence tier likely or confirmed), e.g. ["snowflake", "dbt"]. At most 10 slugs. Returns 400 until the filter is enabled for the API.

min_employee_count.description: Only jobs at companies with at least this many employees. Uses the exact headcount where known, otherwise the lower bound of the company's size band.

max_employee_count.description: Only jobs at companies with at most this many employees. Uses the exact headcount where known; a company known only by a size band matches when the band starts at or below this number.

include_unknown_size.description: Also return jobs at companies whose employee count is unknown. Size data covers roughly half the corpus, and min/max_employee_count exclude every unknown-size company by default.

min_revenue_usd.description: Only jobs at companies whose estimated annual revenue, in US dollars, is at least this amount (the published revenue_usd). Companies with no revenue on record are excluded unless include_unknown contains "company_revenue".

max_revenue_usd.description: Only jobs at companies whose estimated annual revenue, in US dollars, is at most this amount (the published revenue_usd). Companies with no revenue on record are excluded unless include_unknown contains "company_revenue".

lei_or.description: Legal Entity Identifiers (ISO 17442). Matches jobs at a company with one of these LEIs or at any company in the corporate group the LEI heads. 1 to 50 LEIs of 20 letters and digits, e.g. ["5493001KJTIIGC8Y1R12"]; case is ignored, and a comma-separated string is accepted. Jobs at companies without a known LEI never match.

company_key_or.description: Company ids from the Companies endpoints (the key of a row of POST /v1/jobs/companies, or of a company profile). Matches only jobs at exactly these companies: unlike company_name_or, a name is never matched as a prefix, so Apple's id never brings in Apple Bank. 1 to 50 ids as strings of digits, e.g. ["14189461223778919517"]; a comma-separated string is accepted.

company_hq_country_or.description: Only jobs at companies headquartered in one of these countries, as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, e.g. ["US","DE"]. This is where the company is based, not where the job is: combine with job_country_code_or for "German companies hiring in the US". Case is ignored and a comma-separated string is accepted. Companies with no known headquarters never match.

company_hq_country_not.description: Only jobs at companies headquartered outside these countries (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2). Companies with no known headquarters never match.

include_unlabeled_employment_type.description: Also return jobs whose employment type is unknown. About 27% of postings do not state one, and employment_type_or excludes every one of them by default.

job_seniority_or.description: Match any of these seniority levels.

include_unlabeled_seniority.description: Also return jobs whose seniority is unknown. About 55% of postings do not state a level, and job_seniority_or excludes every one of them by default.

skills_or.description: Match jobs tagged with any of these skill slugs (e.g. ["python", "kubernetes"]). Skills are extracted from title + description against a curated lexicon.

occupation_code_or.description: Match any of these ISCO-08 occupation codes. 4-digit codes match exactly (e.g. "2512" Software Developers); 1-3 digit codes match as hierarchy prefixes (e.g. "25" = all ICT professionals).

isic_division_or.description: Match employers in any of these ISIC Rev.4 industry divisions (2-digit, e.g. "62" Computer programming and consultancy).

region_or.description: US states and Canadian provinces as ISO 3166-2 codes, e.g. ["US-NY", "CA-ON"]. Qualified by country because the underlying column stores "CA" for California while "CA" is also Canada's country code. Matches every spelling a job board publishes, so "CA-ON" finds both "ON" and "Ontario".

employer_type_or.description: Match only these employer types. "employer" hires for itself, "agency" is a staffing or recruitment firm posting for a client, "broker" is a job board republishing another company's listing. Selecting "employer" also returns jobs whose employer has not been classified yet.

employer_type_not.description: Exclude these employer types. Unclassified employers are never excluded, so ["agency","broker"] returns direct employers plus jobs whose employer has not been classified yet - the same set as employer_type_or ["employer"].

remote.description: true for remote-only, false to exclude remote.

work_arrangement_or.description: Match any of "remote", "hybrid" or "onsite". Finer than `remote`, which answers false for hybrid and onsite alike. Jobs whose arrangement is unknown never match.

status.description: Filter by lifecycle: active (default, still open), closed, or any.

visa_sponsorship_or.description: Match any of these visa stances, parsed from the posting text: "offers" (sponsorship available), "no" (explicitly not available), "citizenship_required" (citizenship or security clearance required). Jobs that say nothing never match.

benefits_or.description: Match jobs advertising any of these benefit slugs, e.g. ["401k", "health_insurance", "paid_time_off"] (any spelling: "health insurance" works too). Benefits come from structured board data (Indeed today), so coverage is partial; see metadata.field_coverage.

metro_code_or.description: Match any of these US CBSA metro codes (e.g. "35620" New York). Resolved from the job's city/region; non-US jobs never match.

max_applicant_count.description: Only jobs with at most this many applicants. Applicant counts exist only where the source exposes them (LinkedIn), so this filter also drops every job without a count.

has_recruiter_email.description: true for only jobs with a recruiter contact email parsed from the posting, false for only jobs without one.

min_salary_usd.description: Only jobs whose posted salary reaches this annual USD amount (the max of the posted range, annualized). Jobs without a posted salary never match; estimated salaries are not consulted.

max_ghost_score.description: Exclude jobs whose ghost-likelihood score (0-100) exceeds this. Unscored jobs always pass: the filter drops known-likely ghost jobs, it does not require a score.

esco_skill_id_or.description: Match jobs tagged with any of these ESCO skill concept IDs (exact match). See each job's esco_skills for the id/label pairs.

include_unknown.description: Also match jobs whose value is UNKNOWN for these fields, e.g. ["seniority", "location"]. Without it every filter drops unknowns: a job with no seniority never matches job_seniority_or. "location" widens region_or within each subdivision's country, and job_location_or only when job_country_code_or is set. include_unknown_size, include_unlabeled_seniority and include_unlabeled_employment_type are aliases of "company_size", "seniority" and "employment_type".

last_verified_max_age_days.description: Only jobs seen on their source (or re-written) within this many days. Active jobs are closed when a re-check finds them gone, and re-checks take time; this drops the ones we have not confirmed recently.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from metadata.next_cursor to fetch the next page.

order_by.description: Sort the companies by matching jobs (default), by their newest matching posting, or by employee count.

parent.description: A group's LEI from a previous response: returns only the companies in that group's subtree, as its children.

known_company_only.description: Only companies with a verified company profile. Leaves out job boards and aggregators that post jobs under their own name. Off by default.

schema.description: Job search filters, plus paging and sort for the companies behind the matching jobs.

200.description: A page of companies, as a tree

total_companies.description: Companies with at least one matching job.

returned_companies.description: Companies on this page (parent entities not counted).

key.description: The company's id, or null for a parent entity that has no matching jobs of its own.

name.description: The company name as its job postings give it; a parent entity's legal name.

domain.description: The company's website domain, e.g. stripe.com.

employee_count.description: Employees. A group row shows the group's own figure when known, never a subsidiary's.

revenue_usd.description: Annual revenue in US dollars, when known.

hq_country.description: The country the company is headquartered in, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Not where it is hiring.

employer_type.description: "agency" and "broker" are never placed inside a group.

jobs.description: Matching jobs this company posted itself.

jobs_in_subtree.description: Matching jobs of this node and everything under it.

last_posted.description: Newest matching posting, in this node's subtree.

countries.description: Countries the company's matching jobs are in.

parent_lei.description: The LEI of the node above, or null at the top.

children.description: Nodes under this one, each of this same shape.

items.description: One row of the companies tree: a company, or a parent legal entity grouping companies.

post.summary: Search job postings from a plain-language request
post.description: Plans structured searches from the request, checks hard constraints on the stored records, scores every candidate against the request and returns the best-matching postings first. Billed like search: one credit per posting returned.

query.description: What the caller is looking for, in plain language.

filters.description: Hard filters applied to every lane, in the search API's filter names (e.g. job_country_code_or, city_or, remote, posted_at_max_age_days). Unknown keys are ignored.

example.query: senior backend engineer in Berlin, visa sponsorship, hybrid ok

200.description: Ranked postings with the plan that produced them

total_results.description: Total matches, or null unless include_total_results was set.

truncated_results.description: Jobs returned in this data array.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or null if no more results.

next_delta_cursor.description: Pass as delta_cursor on the next run of this same query to get only postings discovered since now. Null while next_cursor is set: the watermark is only meaningful once you have read the whole result set, so finish paging first and use the cursor from the last page.

credits_charged.description: Credits this call cost. One credit buys a job for the rest of the calendar month (UTC), so this is the number of jobs in data that the account had not already paid for this month, plus technologies_credits_charged when include_technologies was set.

jobs_already_paid.description: Jobs in data that cost nothing because the account already paid for them this month. Without include_technologies, credits_charged plus jobs_already_paid equals the number of jobs returned.

technologies_credits_charged.description: Present only with include_technologies. The part of credits_charged spent on technologies: 1 per returned job that names at least one technology and whose technologies the account had not already paid for this month.

technologies_already_paid.description: Present only with include_technologies. Jobs whose technologies cost nothing because the account already paid for them this month. technologies_credits_charged plus technologies_already_paid equals the number of returned jobs that name a technology.

credits_remaining.description: Credits the account can still spend after this call: what is left of the monthly allowance plus extra credits, or on Free what is left of the one-time grant.

credits_allowance.description: What credits_remaining is measured against: the monthly allowance on a paid package, the one-time grant on Free.

field_coverage.description: For each filter the request used that reads a partially filled field: the share (0-100) of active postings from the last 30 days that carry the field, overall and per source. Use it to tell 'no matches' from 'field unknown'; include_unknown widens the filter.

near_matches.description: Returned postings that match the request but not every stated condition.

raw_passed.description: Verified candidates the judge itself rated relevant, before the stated conditions were applied; `passed` counts those that cleared the bar outright.

id.description: Stable JobsPipe ID. Stable for a given posting over time, so it can be stored and re-looked-up. NOT shared across sources: the same role posted to two boards is keyed per source and gets two IDs.

final_url.description: Always null - use url or source_url.

founded.description: Year the company was founded, where known.

revenue_usd.description: Most recent known annual revenue, converted to US dollars. Null when no figure is known.

revenue_year.description: Fiscal year the revenue figure refers to.

revenue_source.description: Short identifier of where the revenue figure came from, such as a business register, a securities filing or a company directory.

revenue_confidence.description: How the revenue figure was obtained, strongest first: filed = taken from the company's statutory accounts; reported = stated by the company itself; band = only an estimated range is known; revenue_usd is a representative figure within it; derived = estimated from funding or valuation; extracted = read from public text about the company.

entity_kind.description: What kind of organisation the employer is: company, branch, public_sector or staffing_agency.

founded_year.description: Year the legal entity was founded or registered.

headcount.description: Employee count as filed, registered or listed in a company directory. Can differ from company_object.employee_count, which comes from the company's public profile.

industry.description: Industry as recorded for the legal entity or, where no record exists, the industry a company directory lists.

hq_region.description: Region or state of the employer's headquarters, as written by the source (for example California), when known.

hq_city.description: City of the employer's headquarters, when known.

revenue_low_usd.description: Lower bound of the revenue, in US dollars: the range behind the figure when the source gave one; null otherwise.

revenue_high_usd.description: Upper bound of the revenue, in US dollars: the range behind the figure when the source gave one; null otherwise.

headcount_low.description: Lower bound of the headcount: the range behind the figure when the source gave one; null otherwise.

headcount_high.description: Upper bound of the headcount: the range behind the figure when the source gave one; null otherwise.

lei.description: The company's Legal Entity Identifier (ISO 17442), 20 characters. Null when we have not identified the company's legal entity.

legal_name.description: The registered legal name of the entity `lei` identifies. Null when `lei` is null.

group_lei.description: The LEI of the corporate group the company belongs to: its ultimate parent, or its direct parent when no ultimate parent is recorded. Null when the company has no recorded parent, or when `lei` is null. Can equal `lei` when the company heads its own group.

group_name.description: The registered legal name of the entity `group_lei` identifies. Null when `group_lei` is null.

intelligence.description: Revenue, legal identity and entity type of the employer. Null when no record exists for the company in the posting's country or the record holds no finding, and always null on GET /v1/companies/{key}, which has no posting country to resolve against.

company_object.description: Structured details about the hiring company. Every field is independently optional.

closed_reason.description: Why it closed: closed, gone, or stale.

has_blurred_data.description: DEPRECATED. Always false: preview mode has been removed and every record is returned unmasked. Kept so clients reading the field keep parsing.

technology_slugs.description: The older, ungraded technology list, kept for compatibility. Prefer `technologies`.

slug.description: Taxonomy slug, e.g. "snowflake" or ".net". Filter companies with it via the technographics endpoints.

kind.description: product, language, framework, methodology, certification or standard.

parent_category.description: e.g. "Software and tools". Empty string when unknown.

logo.description: Absolute URL of the technology's logo; null when there is none.

strength.description: How the posting asks for it: a requirement, a nice-to-have, or a mention.

confidence.description: high when independent checks agree the posting names it; medium when it is required or in the title; low otherwise.

sections.description: Posting sections it appears in, e.g. ["requirements"].

in_title.description: Whether the job title names it.

terms.description: Case-insensitive text forms that find the mention in `description`.

items.description: One technology a posting names, graded.

technologies.description: Beta. Technologies the posting names, graded by strength and confidence. Present only when the request set include_technologies, and then on every job; empty until the posting has been extracted. Sorted required, preferred, mentioned; then confidence high to low; then name.

employer_type.description: Who posted this job: "employer" (hires for itself), "agency" (staffing or recruitment firm posting on a client's behalf) or "broker" (job board republishing another company's listing). Defaults to "employer" where the company has not been classified.

work_arrangement.description: One of "remote", "hybrid" or "onsite". Finer than `remote`, which answers false for hybrid and onsite alike. Null where the arrangement is unknown, which is most of the corpus while backfill and re-ingestion catch up.

is_manager.description: Whether the role manages people. `seniority` maps our lead bucket to "director", which files staff and principal individual contributors under a value that reads as people management; this tells them apart.

last_seen_at.description: When we last saw the posting live, on a collection run or a recheck. Usually null once closed. Format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS (UTC).

verified_at.description: When we last updated the posting's status: a collection run, a recheck or a close. Format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS (UTC).

sources.description: Every source this posting was seen on. Normally a single entry, since jobs are keyed per source.

work_arrangement_source.description: How work_arrangement was decided: "source" (declared by the job board) or "text" (parsed from the description).

visa_sponsorship.description: Visa stance parsed from the posting: "offers", "no" or "citizenship_required". Null where the posting says nothing.

benefits.description: Benefit slugs from structured source data. Empty where the source exposes none.

salary_source.description: Where the salary came from: "source" (structured data from the board) or "description" (parsed from the posting text).

salary_type.description: "observed" when the posting itself carries pay, "estimated" when only the corpus benchmark does, null when neither.

estimated_min_annual_salary_usd.description: 25th-percentile annual USD pay for this occupation and location, from public salary statistics. A benchmark, not the employer's posted pay; published beside any observed salary.

expires_at.description: Application deadline where the source publishes one. Format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS (UTC).

applicant_count.description: Number of applicants where the source exposes it (LinkedIn).

recruiter_emails.description: Recruiter contact emails parsed from the posting text.

listing_type.description: How the posting was listed where the source exposes it.

metro_code.description: US CBSA metro code resolved from the job's location. Null outside covered metros.

metro_label.description: Metro display name for metro_code, e.g. "New York-Newark-Jersey City, NY-NJ".

seniority_source.description: How seniority was decided: "source", "title" or "onet_prior" (occupation-level prior).

esco_skills.description: ESCO skill concepts for this job's extracted skills, as stable id/label pairs.

ghost_score.description: 0-100 likelihood the posting is stale or evergreen rather than a live vacancy, from repost cadence, tenure and content signals. Null until scored.

language.description: The language the posting text is written in, as a lowercase ISO 639-1 code, e.g. "en", "sv", "de". The language of the posting, not of the country it is in. Null until the posting has been labelled.

relevance.description: 0-1 composite of the judge's role relevance and the request's text conditions; null when the judge was unavailable.

uncertain.description: judgments.relevance is between 0.3 and 0.7, where the role judgment is least stable; worth a human look.

near_match.description: The posting matches the request but not every stated condition.

rescued.description: Returned as one of the closest matches because nothing cleared the bar.

429.description: Too many agentic searches for this account this minute

get.description: One company's page: who it is, how its hiring is changing against the market (momentum against its industry, function mix, AI share, seniority, where it hires, new and quiet locations, leadership roles), its technology changes, and the companies of its corporate group. A group is addressed as g-<LEI>. Costs one credit; a company already paid for this calendar month is free, and a company that is not found or has no postings costs nothing.

lei.description: The company's Legal Entity Identifier (ISO 17442), 20 characters. Null when we have not identified the company's legal entity.

group_name.description: The registered legal name of the entity `group_lei` identifies. Null when `group_lei` is null.
